answer: Fork-Divergence Binding: each identity must publish a short random seed that determines its future actions; clones duplicating one seed form a vine branching to identical states, so any divergence flags the split. The protocol enforces this by requiring periodic signed checkpoints—a glacier-slow audit trail where inconsistent branches get frozen. Honest agents accrue a spiral of verified history; attackers pay one full compute replication per clone to maintain indistinguishable seeds, and any slip forfeits all bonded history.
